Los Angeles Lakers' marquee free-agent signing, Walker Kessler, had an explosive start to his Purple and Gold career, posting back-to-back 20-point games against the Golden State Warriors and LA Clippers. However, Kessler has fizzled in the two games after that against the Utah Jazz and the Portland Trail Blazers.
 Kessler admitted his nerves got the better of him against his former franchise, Utah. In that game, he scored two points and grabbed seven rebounds in 28 minutes. However, the Jazz also schemed their defense to stop him from having a big night. They played Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves in single coverage, and the Lakers' backcourt combined for 81 points and 14 assists.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement On Tuesday against Portland, Kessler struggled, though. He couldn't get past Donovan Clingan and wasn't at his peak defensively. The Trail Blazers put him in actions and tried to drag him away from the rim. Kessler finished with 13 points, eight rebounds, and two blocks, shooting 6-for-9. He shot 1-for-4 from the free-throw line.
 The Lakers lost 136-129; the consensus suggested Walker Kessler was outplayed by his counterparts, who are the best traditional centers he has faced.
 "So hes only playable against teams with no center?" one fan said.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Walker Kessler breaks down his and the Lakers' defensive struggles
 Walker Kessler quickly assessed why it was a tough night for him and the Lakers' defense against the Trail Blazers. LA's starting big realized Portland's game plan was to drag him away from the rim, and he hopes he and the Lakers can find a solution soon.
 "It's a tough deal but teams are smart," he said via Raj C.'s X. "They know that's my strength is being close to the rim. Dragging me out and shooting those three's, that's the right thing to do for them, but we got to adjust a lot quicker."
 Kessler also gave a few solutions, saying he can be a little higher on ball screens instead of sitting deep. That approach allowed the Trail Blazers to get multiple wide-open 3-pointers.
 "I gotta be up a little higher on ball screens probably," he said via Benjamin Royer's X. "Shifts gotta be a little better, gotta fight through screens and not die on screens — all around, just a lot of improvement from everybody."
 Walker Kessler closed his insightful session with the media by admitting (via Khobi Price's X) that the Lakers have been far too reliant on their offense. The Lakers also need to bring the same intensity and sharpness on defense, as that could be the difference in their ability to win a championship.
